claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ (the Terraform/OpenTofu state backend guide for Pulumi Cloud) exists.
In self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the API service specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
A separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is not required in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud: PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN, avoiding a second DNS record.

The Terraform/OpenTofu state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the Terraform-compatible API domain in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.

For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value should be used in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name in place of `tf.pulumi.com`.
